verdicts.label: FALSE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: The Government of India has not launched a national 'PM Free Laptop Yojana 2026'. Messages promoting this scheme are fake. While some individual states may have their own local laptop distribution programs, there is no central government scheme to provide free laptops to all students.
verdicts.reasoning_en: Multiple credible sources, including a notice on the official AICTE government website (ws-4) and a PIB Fact Check report cited by Livemint (ws-2), have explicitly stated that the Government of India has not announced any national free laptop scheme. Numerous fact-checking organizations have consistently debunked similar claims over several years (fc-2, fc-3, fc-8). The evidence overwhelmingly indicates that the 'PM Free Laptop Yojana 2026' is not a real government initiative.

verdicts.label: FALSE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: Since the 'PM Free Laptop Yojana 2026' does not exist as a national scheme, there is no application deadline. Scammers often invent urgent deadlines to create a false sense of panic and trick people into sharing their data.
verdicts.reasoning_en: The primary claim of a national 'PM Free Laptop Yojana' has been proven false by government sources (ws-4, ws-2). Therefore, any associated deadline, including October 15, is also false. An article from Careerindia.com (ws-8) explains that such urgent deadlines are a common tactic used in scams. While other unrelated schemes in different regions or countries might have deadlines (ws-10, ws-11), none of the evidence supports an October 15 deadline for a national Indian laptop scheme.

verdicts.label: FALSE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: The website www.pm-free-laptop-yojana.in is not an official government website. Official Indian government websites typically end in '.gov.in' or '.nic.in'.
verdicts.reasoning_en: The claim is false because the 'PM Free Laptop Yojana' itself is a non-existent scheme, as confirmed by government sources (ws-16, ws-17). Furthermore, multiple sources (ws-14, ws-15) clarify that official Indian government websites use specific domains like '.gov.in' or '.nic.in', which the claimed URL does not. The use of a non-standard domain is a key indicator that the website is not legitimate and is likely part of a scam.
